verses.zh: 雅各啊，创造你的耶和华，以色列啊，造成你的那位，现在如此说：你不要害怕！因为我救赎了你。我曾提你的名召你，你是属我的。
verses.en: Now, this is what the Lord says,the one who created you, O Jacob,and formed you, O Israel:“Don’t be afraid, for I will protect[NOTE:1] you.I call you by name, you are mine.
notes: Or “redeem.” See the note at 41:14. Cf. NCV “saved you”; CEV “rescued you”; NLT “ransomed you.”
verses.commentary:
43:1 "Lord" This is from the word YHWH. In Exod. 3:14 it is
translated "I Am." This form is from the Hebrew VERB "to be." He is the ever-living, only-living One.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

▣ "your Creator" This is a Qal PARTICIPLE (BDB 135, KB 153, used only of divine creation, Gen. 1). This
is a common theme throughout the Servant Songs. Here it refers to the establishment of the nation of Israel
(cf. Genesis 12; 15; 22).

The second line of chapter 43 has the parallel VERB "formed" (BDB 427, KB 428,
Qal PARTICIPLE, cf. Isa. 43:21; 44:2,21,24). YHWH was not only the Creator of the physical
realm but also the covenant people (cf. Genesis 12; 15; 18; 22).

▣ "O Jacob. . .O Israel" These two VOCATIVES both refer to the collective
covenant people, the seed of Abraham.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

▣ "Do not fear" This is a command (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense). So often this is God's word for His people, especially after
the exile and destruction of Jerusalem and the temple (cf. Isa. 40:9; 41:10,13,14; 44:2; 54:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

▣ "redeemed" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM.

▣ "I have called you by name" This (both "redeemed" and "called" are Qal
PERFECTS) refers to God's choice of Israel (cf. Isa. 43:7; 45:3-4). This was a special
calling through Abraham (cf. Genesis 12; 15; 18; 22).

Naming something shows ones power and authority.

- Adam names the animals ‒ Gen. 2:19-20

- Adam names Eve ‒ Gen. 2:23; 3:20

- YHWH names the stars ‒ Ps. 147:4; Isa. 40:26; 48:12-13

- YHWH names His people ‒ Isa. 43:1,7; 45:3-4

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

▣ "you are Mine" See Isa. 43:21 and Exod. 19:5-6. Israel was uniquely YHWH's people.

verses.zh: 你从水中经过，我必与你同在；你蹚过江河，水必不漫过你；你从火中行过，必不被烧，火焰也不着在你身上。
verses.en: When you pass through the waters, I am with you;when you pass[NOTE:1] through the streams, they will not overwhelm you.When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned;the flames will not harm[NOTE:2] you.
notes: The verb is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
Heb “burn” (so NASB); NAB, NRSV, NLT “consume”; NIV “set you ablaze.”
verses.commentary:
43:2 "the waters. . .the fire. . .the flame" This is such a wonderful text! These are used as
imagery of problems, fears, and foes! Oh, what wonderful truth for believers in a fallen world!

▣ "will be with you" This is God's greatest promise (i.e. His personal presence,
cf. Isa. 43:5; Deut. 31:6,8; Ps. 23:4; Matt. 28:20). This is what the Messianic title "Immanauel"
means (cf. Isa. 7:14).

▣ "Nor will the flame burn you" For a powerful example see Daniel 3.

verses.zh: 因为我是耶和华―你的　神，是以色列的圣者―你的救主；我已经使埃及作你的赎价，使古实和西巴代替你。
verses.en: For I am the Lord your God,the Holy One of Israel,[NOTE:1] your deliverer.I have handed over Egypt as a ransom price,Ethiopia and Seba[NOTE:2] in place of you.
notes: See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.
Seba is not the same as Sheba in southern Arabia; cf. Gen 1:10; 1 Chr 1:9.
verses.commentary:
43:3 "Savior" This root's basic meaning can be translated "to be wide" (BDB 446, KB 448,
Hiphil PARTICIPLE). The names Joshua, Hosea, and Jesus are based on this root.

SPECIAL TOPIC: OUR SAVIOR

▣ "ransom" This speaks of the high cost of redemption. The object of this verse
seems to be Cyrus II's conquests.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

verses.zh: 因我看你为宝为尊；又因我爱你，所以我使人代替你，使列邦人替换你的生命。
verses.en: Since you are precious and special in my sight[NOTE:1] and I love you,I will hand over people in place of you,nations in place of your life.
notes: Heb “Since you are precious in my eyes and you are honored.”
verses.commentary:
43:4 There is an apparent parallel between

- Isa. 43:3 ‒ a Divine ransom involving Egypt, Cush, and Seba instead of Israel

- Isa. 43:4 ‒ a Divine ransom involving

- other men (Adam, BDB 9)

- other peoples (BDB 522)

- The UBS Text Project (p. 111) gives another option (i.e. Assyria. . .Edom), which is found in
the REB. This change is possible without a change of consonants. However, the UBS Text
Project rates option #1 as A (very high probability).

Verses 3 and 4 are a literary way of showing YHWH's great love for Israel and
His willingness for Cyrus' military victories to assure Israel's return to Palestine.

43: 5-7 This reflects the return from Neo-Babylonian exile allowed by Cyrus II's decree
(538 B.C.), which allowed all the exiled people groups to return to their homeland.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF PERSIA, C.

verses.zh: 不要害怕，因我与你同在；我必领你的后裔从东方来，又从西方招聚你。
verses.en: Don’t be afraid, for I am with you.From the east I will bring your descendants;from the west I will gather you.

verses.zh: 我要对北方说，交出来！对南方说，不要拘留！将我的众子从远方带来，将我的众女从地极领回，
verses.en: I will say to the north, ‘Hand them over!’and to the south, ‘Don’t hold any back!’Bring my sons from distant lands,and my daughters from the remote regions of the earth,

verses.zh: 就是凡称为我名下的人，是我为自己的荣耀创造的，是我所做成，所造作的。
verses.en: everyone who belongs to me,[NOTE:1] whom I created for my glory,whom I formed—yes, whom I made”.
notes: Heb “everyone who is called by my name” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
43:7 "called. . .created. . .formed. . .made" God had a purpose for Israel (cf. Isa. 43:10;
Gen. 12:1-3; Exod. 19:5-6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 你要将有眼而瞎、有耳而聋的民都带出来！
verses.en: Bring out the people who are blind, even though they have eyes,those who are deaf, even though they have ears!
verses.commentary:
43:8 "the people who are blind" This was because of their continuing unbelief and
covenant disobedience (cf. Isa. 6:9-10 and 42:18-22).

verses.zh: 任凭万国聚集；任凭众民会合。其中谁能将此声明，并将先前的事说给我们听呢？他们可以带出见证来，自显为是；或者他们听见便说：这是真的。
verses.en: All nations gather together,the peoples assemble.Who among them announced this?Who predicted earlier events for us?[NOTE:1] Let them produce their witnesses to testify they were right;let them listen and affirm, “It is true.”
notes: Heb “and the former things he was causing us to hear?”
verses.commentary:
43:9 There is a series of Qal IMPERFECTS used as
JUSSIVES (cf. NRSV and NJB, "let. . .").

- let them bring their witness (BDB 678, KB 733)

- let them justify themselves (BDB 842, KB 1003)

- let them hear (BDB 1033, KB 1570)

- let them say (BDB 55, KB 65)

The nations, like the idols of Isaiah 40, do not know the future. Only YHWH holds
time and history in His hand (i.e. many predictions in Isaiah of the fall of Assyria and Babylon). He
will use Israel to reveal Himself and ultimately He will use the Messiah, His special Servant to
bring the nations to faith (i.e. Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8).

verses.zh: 耶和华说：你们是我的见证，我所拣选的仆人。既是这样，便可以知道，且信服我，又明白我就是耶和华。在我以前没有真神（真：原文是造作的）；在我以后也必没有。
verses.en: “You are my witnesses,” says the Lord,“my servant whom I have chosenso that you may consider[NOTE:1] and believe in me,and understand that I am he.No god was formed before me,and none will outlive me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “know” (KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).
Heb “and after me, there will not be”; NASB “there will be none after Me.”
verses.commentary:
43:10-13 Notice the many ways YHWH's uniqueness, power, and eternality are expressed.

- He wants humans, made in His image (cf. Gen. 1:26-27), to

- know (BDB 393, KB 390, Qal IMPERFECT; see SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW)

- believe (BDB 52, KB 63, Hiphil IMPERFECT; see SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS [OT])

- understand (BDB 106, KB 122, Qal IMPERFECT)

- He is the only God (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM)

- I am He, Isa. 43:10,11,12,13

- before Me there was no God formed, Isa. 43:10

- after Me no God formed, Isa. 43:10

- no savior beside Me, Isa. 43:11; 45:22

- His acts (all Hiphil IMPERFECTS; see wonderful parallel at Ps. 103:6-14)

- He has spoken (BDB 616, KB 665)

- He has saved (BDB 446, KB 448)

- He has proclaimed (BDB 1033, KB 1570)

- He is from eternity, Isa. 43:13a; Micah 5:3; Ps. 90:2

- His power, Isa. 43:13b,c

These truths are what the nations need to know and affirm, Isa. 43:9.

43:10 "You are My witnesses" This is imagery for a court scene (cf. Isa. 43:12; 1:18; 41:21; 44:8;
Rom. 8:31-39; Matt. 25:31-46), where all the nations are gathered (cf. Isa. 43:9).

▣ "Before Me there was no God" This refers to monotheism (cf. Isa. 43:10-13). This
is reflected in Exod. 20:5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

verses.zh: 惟有我是耶和华；除我以外没有救主。
verses.en: I, I am the Lord,and there is no deliverer besides me.

verses.zh: 我曾指示，我曾拯救，我曾说明，并且在你们中间没有别神。所以耶和华说：你们是我的见证。我也是　神；
verses.en: I decreed and delivered and proclaimed,and there was no other god among you.You are my witnesses,” says the Lord, “that I am God.

verses.zh: 自从有日子以来，我就是　神；谁也不能救人脱离我手。我要行事谁能阻止呢？
verses.en: From this day forward I am he;no one can deliver from my power;[NOTE:1] I will act, and who can prevent it?”
notes: Heb “hand” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “No one can oppose what I do.”
verses.commentary:
43:13 "eternity" This follows the Septuagint. The MT has "from the day."

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE MASORETIC TEXT

verses.zh: 耶和华―你们的救赎主、以色列的圣者如此说：因你们的缘故，我已经打发人到巴比伦去；并且我要使迦勒底人如逃民，都坐自己喜乐的船下来。
verses.en: This is what the Lord says,your Protector,[NOTE:1] the Holy One of Israel:[NOTE:2] “For your sake I send to Babylonand make them all fugitives,[NOTE:3] turning the Babylonians’ joyful shouts into mourning songs.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “kinsman redeemer.” See the note at 41:14.
See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.
Heb “and I bring down [as] fugitives all of them.”

The Hebrew text reads literally, “as for the Babylonians, in ships their joyful shout.” This might be paraphrased, “even the Babylonians in the ships [over which] they joyfully shouted.” The point would be that the Lord caused the Babylonians to flee for safety in the ships in which they took such great pride. A slight change in vocalization yields the reading “into mourning songs,” which provides a good contrast with “joyful shout.” The prefixed bet (בְּ) would indicate identity.
verses.commentary:
43:14 "the Lord your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel" See
Contextual Insights, G.

▣ "will bring them all down as fugitives" This refers to the fall of Neo-Babylon by
Cyrus II. It was not Cyrus' power that defeated Neo-Babylonians but YHWH's power and purpose
(i.e. "for your sake").

There is a possible revocalization of the Hebrew consonants (BDB 138).

- "fugitives," מברחים, Peshitta, NASB, NKJV,
NET, cf. Ezek. 17:21 only, but possibly Isa. 15:5

- "bars," MT, Ezek. 38:11, בריחים, JPSOA, cf. Isa. 45:2

The UBS Text Project, p. 112, gives option #1 a B rating.

▣ "the Chaldeans" Herodotus (450 B.C.), Hist. I, uses
this term (BDB 505) to refer to an ethnic group (cf. 2 Kgs. 24:1-4; Dan. 5:30) as well as a priestly
class (cf. Dan. 2:2; 3:8; 4:7; 5:7,11) whose usage goes back to Cyrus II. Even before this time
period Assyrian records used the term (BDB 505) in an ethnic sense (cf. R. K. Harrison,
Introduction to the Old Testament, p. 1113). Also read the good discussion of the possibility
of a confusion of two similar terms (i.e. Kal-du vs. Kasdu) in The Expositors Bible
Commentary, vol. 7, pp. 14-15 or Robert Dick Wilson, Studies in the Book of Daniel, series 1.

Because Gen. 11:28 states that Ur of the Chaldeans was the home of Terah and
his family, Chaldeans may have been ethnically Semitic (i.e. same racial group as the Hebrews).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHALDEANS

▣ There is another possible revocalization of the Hebrew consonants.

- into the ships (BDB 58, NASB, NKJV)

- in lamentation (change of vowels, JPSOA, NRSV, NJB, TEV, REB, NET Bible)

- the LXX has "bound in ships"

It is possible that Isa. 43:14 should be taken as Neo-Babylonian people thinking they
could escape the Persian army by floating down river (i.e. Euphrates) in the ships they were so
proud of, yet now they will be ships of mourning!

verses.zh: 我是耶和华―你们的圣者，是创造以色列的，是你们的君王。
verses.en: I am the Lord, your Holy One,[NOTE:1] the one who created Israel, your King.”
notes: See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.
verses.commentary: 43:15 "your King" This is possible linked to 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17. See Contextual Insights, G.

verses.zh: 耶和华在沧海中开道，在大水中开路，
verses.en: This is what the Lord says,the one who made a road through the sea,a pathway through the surging waters,
verses.commentary:
43:16 This uses

- the Exodus from Egypt (cf. Isa. 43:17; Exodus 14-15) as imagery for the return from Neo-Babylon

- YHWH's control of the waters of chaos. See SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

▣ "I will do something new" This theme of something "new" is so common in Isaiah
(cf. Isa. 41:15; 42:9,10; 48:6; 62:2; 65:17; 66:22). See full note at Isa. 62:2.

SPECIAL TOPIC: OLD THINGS. . .NEW THINGS

verses.zh: 使车辆、马匹、军兵、勇士都出来，一同躺下，不再起来；他们灭没，好像熄灭的灯火。
verses.en: the one who led chariots and horses to destruction,[NOTE:1] together with a mighty army.They fell down,[NOTE:2] never to rise again;they were extinguished, put out like a burning wick:
notes: Heb “led out chariots and horses.” The words “to destruction” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The verse refers to the destruction of the Egyptians at the Red Sea.
Heb “lay down”; NAB “lie prostrate together”; CEV “lie dead”; NRSV “they lie down.”

verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：你们不要记念从前的事，也不要思想古时的事。
verses.en: “Don’t remember these earlier events;[NOTE:1] don’t recall these former events.
notes: Heb “the former things” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “forget all that.”

verses.zh: 看哪，我要做一件新事；如今要发现，你们岂不知道吗？我必在旷野开道路，在沙漠开江河。
verses.en: “Look, I am about to do something new.Now it begins to happen![NOTE:1] Do you not recognize[NOTE:2] it?Yes, I will make a road in the wildernessand paths[NOTE:3] in the wastelands.
notes: Heb “sprouts up”; NASB “will spring forth.”
Or “know” (KJV, ASV); NASB “be aware of”; NAB, NIV, NRSV “perceive.”
The Hebrew text has “streams,” probably under the influence of v. 20. The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has נתיבות (“paths”).
verses.commentary:
43:19 "I will even make a roadway in the wilderness" This is a very common biblical theme
(cf. Isa. 40:1-4).

▣

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB, JPSOA, LXX, Peshitta
"Rivers"

REB, DSS
"Paths"

The UBS Text Project, p. 113, cannot decide between the MT, "rivers/streams"
and DSS "paths."

- נהרות ‒ BDB 625, "rivers"

- נתיבות ‒ BDB 677, "paths"

I think option #2 is a better poetic parallel to the previous line of poetry (notice "path," BDB 677,
in v. 16, as well as "a way," BDB 292).

However, v. 20 does involve YHWH bringing water (i.e. rivers, BDB 677) to the desert.

verses.zh: 野地的走兽必尊重我；野狗和鸵鸟也必如此。因我使旷野有水，使沙漠有河，好赐给我的百姓、我的选民喝。
verses.en: The wild animals[NOTE:1] honor me,the jackals and ostriches,because I put water in the wildernessand streams in the wastelandsto quench the thirst of my chosen people,
notes: Heb “animals of the field.”
verses.commentary:
43:20 Instead of curses (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28) the beasts became tame. Nature
blooms and produces in light of YHWH's presence and blessings, imagery of a restored Garden of Eden.

See Isa. 32:20 for a list of passages like this.

verses.zh: 这百姓是我为自己所造的，好述说我的美德。
verses.en: the people whom I formed for myself,so they might praise me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “[so] they might declare my praise.”

verses.zh: 雅各啊，你并没有求告我；以色列啊，你倒厌烦我。
verses.en: “But you did not call for me, O Jacob;you did not long[NOTE:1] for me, O Israel.
notes: Or “strive”; KJV, ASV, NRSV “been weary of me.”
verses.commentary:
43:22-24 This is not a condemnation of sacrifice in general but of false motives (JPOSOA footnote,
cf. Jeremiah 7; Amos 5). The VERBS are all PERFECTS which show a
settled attitude of rebellion.

43:22 These are acts of worship done at the temple.

verses.zh: 你没有将你的羊带来给我作燔祭，也没有用祭物尊敬我；我没有因供物使你服劳，也没有因乳香使你厌烦。
verses.en: You did not bring me lambs for your burnt offerings;you did not honor me with your sacrifices.I did not burden you with offerings;I did not make you weary by demanding[NOTE:1] incense.
notes: Heb “with.” The words “by demanding” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 你没有用银子为我买菖蒲，也没有用祭物的脂油使我饱足；倒使我因你的罪恶服劳，使我因你的罪孽厌烦。
verses.en: You did not buy me aromatic reeds;[NOTE:1] you did not present to me[NOTE:2] the fat of your sacrifices.Yet you burdened me with your sins;you made me weary with your evil deeds.[NOTE:3]
notes: That is, “calamus” (so NIV); NCV, TEV, NLT “incense”; CEV “spices.”
Heb “you did not saturate me”; NASB “Neither have you filled Me.”

In vv. 22-24 the Lord appears to be condemning his people for failure to bring the proper sacrifices. However, this is problematic. If this refers to the nation’s behavior while in exile, such cultic service was impossible and could hardly be expected by the Lord. If this refers to the nation’s conduct before the exile, it contradicts other passages that depict Israel as bringing excessive sacrifices (see, e.g., Isa 1:11-14; Jer 6:20; Amos 4:4-5; 5:21-23). Rather than being a condemnation of Israel’s failure to bring sacrifices, these verses are better taken as a highly rhetorical comment on the worthlessness of Israel’s religious ritual. They may have brought sacrifices, but not to the Lord, for he did not accept them or even want them. See C. R. North, Second Isaiah, 127, and R. Whybray, Isaiah 40-66 (NCBC), 91.
verses.commentary:
43:24 "sweet cane" This (BDB 889) refers to holy anointing oil (cf. Exod. 30:23; Jer. 6:20).

▣ "sins. . .iniquities" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT, A. #1, #2

verses.zh: 惟有我为自己的缘故涂抹你的过犯；我也不记念你的罪恶。
verses.en: I, I am the one who blots out your rebellious deeds for my sake;your sins I do not remember.
verses.commentary:
43:25 "I, even I, am the one who wipes out your transgressions for My own sake" God's forgiveness
is an act of pure grace, not merit (cf. Isa. 37:35; 48:9,11; Ezek. 36:22-36; Eph. 2:8-9).

▣ "I will not remember your sins" When God forgives, God forgets (cf. Isa. 1:18; 38:17;
44:22; Ps. 103:12; Micah 7:19)! What a needed truth in light of Satan's continuing condemnations! Oh
the mercy and grace of God!

SPECIAL TOPIC: WORDS FOR FORGIVENESS

verses.zh: 你要提醒我，你我可以一同辩论；你可以将你的理陈明，自显为义。
verses.en: Remind me of what happened. Let’s debate!You, prove to me that you are right![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “you, tell in order that you may be right”; NAB “prove your innocence.”
verses.commentary:
43:26 "let us argue our case together" This reflects a legal imagery of a court room
(cf. Isa. 1:18; 41:21; Rom. 8:31-39). This verse has a series of commands by the judge.

- put Me in remembrance ‒ BDB 269, KB 269, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- let us argue our case together ‒ BDB 1047, KB 1627, Niphal COHORTATIVE

- state your case ‒ BDB 707, KB 765, Piel IMPERATIVE

verses.zh: 你的始祖犯罪；你的师傅违背我。
verses.en: The father of your nation[NOTE:1] sinned;your spokesmen[NOTE:2] rebelled against me.
notes: Heb “your first father.” This could refer to Abraham (see 51:2), but elsewhere in Isaiah he does not appear in a negative light (see 29:22; 41:8; 63:16). A more likely candidate is Jacob/Israel, also referred to as the nation’s “father” elsewhere (see 58:14; 63:16).
On the meaning of the term לִיץ (lits), see HALOT 590 s.v. מֵלִיץ. This may refer to the nation’s prophets, priests, and/or kings.
verses.commentary:
43:27 "Your first forefather sinned" Literally it is "father." It could refer to Adam or Jacob or
any Jewish ancestor. It shows that God's love is undeserved. The OT does not dwell on the origin of
sin, but acknowledges its presence and pervasiveness. On the origin of "sin" some rabbis, like Paul,
emphasize Genesis 3, but most emphasize Genesis 6 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: "sons of God" in Genesis 6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE AGE OF ACCOUNTABILITY

▣ "spokesmen" This is a reference to either

- the prophets

- the priests or Levites (cf. 2 Chr. 30:22)

- the civil leaders

verses.zh: 所以，我要辱没圣所的首领，使雅各成为咒诅，使以色列成为辱骂。
verses.en: So I defiled your holy princes,and handed Jacob over to destruction,and subjected[NOTE:1] Israel to humiliating abuse.
notes: The word “subjected” is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
43:28 "I will pollute the princes of the sanctuary" The VERB "pollute"
(BDB 320 III, KB 319, Piel IMPERFECT with waw) can mean "pollute,"
defile," or "profane." The NEB and REB slightly change the Hebrew consonants to "your princes
profaned my sanctuary," which follows the LXX.

It is uncertain whether the two VERBS of Isa. 43:28 refer to the past
or the future. The Hebrew text links verses 27 and 28. Verse 28 obviously refers to the past. Most of
chapter 43 deals with YHWH's current deliverance of Israel from exile. Hebrew TENSES
do not give time, just action; time must be ascertained from the context.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW GRAMMAR, II. A.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Israel's unique position as YHWH's covenant people is clearly revealed in Isa. 43:1-7.

- He formed them, Isa. 43:1,7

- He redeemed them, Isa. 43:1

- He called them by His name, Isa. 43:1,7

- He protected them, Isa. 43:2

- He is their covenant God, Isa. 43:3

- They are precious in His sight, Isa. 43:4

- He honored them, Isa. 43:4

- He loved them, Isa. 43:4

- He is with them, Isa. 43:5

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

- YHWH wants to use them to reveal Himself to the nations, Isa. 43:8-10 (esp. Isa. 43:10c).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

- Verses 10d-f ‒ 13 are a theological affirmation of YHWH's uniqueness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

- YHWH will bring His people back from exile (Isa. 43:5-6,14,16,19-20)

- through Cyrus II's decree in 538 B.C. (imagery of a second Exodus)

- ultimately through the Messiah (a third and final exodus from sin)

- YHWH will redeem Israel even though they do not deserve it (cf. Isa. 43:22-24). However,
this will involve a "new covenant" (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 35:22-36). YHWH has a worldwide
redemptive plan

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

- YHWH as Israel's redeemer is the focus of this chapter (cf. Isa. 43:1,3,11,14,25-26). YHWH
acts because of who He is and for His greater purpose. Israel is a precious tool in the hand of
God for universal redemption.

- Names for God used in chapter 43 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C. D.)

- "the Lord" (Isa. 43:1,3,11,14) YHWH ‒ The
covenant name for God (cf. Exod. 3:14), "I Am," is from the Hebrew VERB "to be."

- "God" (Isa. 43:3; "El in Isa. 43:13) Elohim ‒ This is a PLURAL
word. The rabbis say YHWH is God's name for mercy, while Elohim deals with the world in
general (i.e. creator, sustainer). These two names for God are the most common in the OT.

I reject the modern western model of "Source Criticism" that turns these names into separate authors.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PENTATEUCH SOURCE CRITICISM (J.E.D.P.)

- "The Holy One of Israel" (Isa. 43:3,15) ‒ This title expresses God's purity and
transcendance (see note at Isa. 40:25; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE).

- "Savior" (Isa. 43:3,11,12) Yasha ‒ This is from the same root as
Joshua and Jesus. The basic meaning is "to be wide" or "spacious" (cf. Isa. 19:20; 45:15,21;
49:26; 60:16; 63:8; see SPECIAL TOPIC: OUR SAVIOR).

- "Redeemer" (Isa. 43:14) ‒ This is from the same root as Go'el, the
kinsman redeemer or avenger (cf. Ruth 4:4,6). This term depicts God as our near kinsman
(cf. Isa. 41:14; 44:6,24; 47:4; 48:17; 49:7,26; 54:5,8; 59:20; 60:16; 63:16). It is another example
of God's personal relationship with us. Other examples are God as parent or husband. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

- "The Creator" (Isa. 43:15) ‒ YHWH the creator (cf. Isa. 40:28) is also the
special covenant God of Israel. This (the VERB bara, cf. Isa. 43:1) is a
common theme (cf. Isaiah 40-66).

- "King" (Isa. 43:15) ‒ God is the true King of Israel. The earthly king is
merely His representative (cf. 1 Samuel 8). See See SPECIAL TOPIC: TITLES FOR THE SPECIAL COMING ONE
